title: Transportation
subtitle: Write your transportation problem below or load it from a file.

hint.northwest: Starts at the top-left cell and moves on as supply and demand run out.
hint.minCost: Assigns as much as possible to the cheapest cell that is still available.
hint.vogel: Uses penalties (difference between the two lowest costs) to decide where to allocate first.

editor.hint: Fill in the unit costs (center), the supply of each source (right column) and the demand of each destination (bottom row).

balance.balanced: Balanced problem: total supply = total demand = {{total}}.
balance.moreSupply: Total supply ({{supply}}) is greater than total demand ({{demand}}): {{diff}} units of supply will be left over. To balance it, add a dummy destination with demand {{diff}} and cost 0.
balance.moreDemand: Total demand ({{demand}}) is greater than total supply ({{supply}}): {{diff}} units will be missing. To balance it, add a dummy source with supply {{diff}} and cost 0.

step.title: Step {{n}}
step.initial: Initial table: unit costs, supply (right) and demand (bottom).
step.northwest: Northwest corner: start at cell (1, 1); then, if the row's supply ran out, move down a row; if the column's demand ran out, move one column to the right. Chosen cell: source {{i}} → destination {{j}}.
step.minCost: Least cost: among the cells still available (row and column not exhausted), the one with the lowest unit cost is {{cost}}: source {{i}} → destination {{j}}.
step.vogel: Vogel's approximation: for every open row and column the penalty (second-lowest cost − lowest cost) is computed. The largest penalty is {{penalty}}, in {{type}} {{index}}. In it we pick the cell with the lowest cost: source {{i}} → destination {{j}}.
step.allocate: We allocate as much as possible: $\min(\text{supply}, \text{demand}) = \min({{supply}}, {{demand}}) = {{amount}}$ units.
step.exhaustedRow: The supply of source {{i}} is exhausted: the row is crossed out.
step.exhaustedColumn: The demand of destination {{j}} is satisfied: the column is crossed out.
step.exhaustedBoth: The supply of source {{i}} and the demand of destination {{j}} ran out at the same time (degenerate solution): both the row and the column are crossed out.
step.done: Done: all the supply or all the demand has been met.
step.clickHint: Tip: in step-by-step mode, click a free cell to choose it yourself.
